layout_map:
1. Outer dark app frame / canvas background surrounding the slide.
2. Slide header bar: light gray strip containing the centered title "Polynomial Kernel" and the slide number "27" inside a yellow circle at the top-right.
3. Main slide body: white rectangle with rounded corners and a blue border containing all math content.
4. Top-left math block: vector definitions a and b with red and blue column-vector components.
5. Top-right "Remember:" callout: gray-filled box with the identity (aᵀb)² = ... expansion reminder.
6. Middle expansion block: two-line derivation of (aᵀb + 1)² spanning the full width.
7. Bottom feature-mapping block: row vector × matrix = φ(a)ᵀφ(b), a "Where: φ(x) ≡" definition, and a tall column vector on the far right mapping to 6D, with "2D ⇒ 6D" in red at the bottom-right corner.
first_glance_test: Within 3 seconds a new user sees a dark app frame containing a light, worksheet-style math slide titled "Polynomial Kernel." The screen offers zero visible actions — no navigation, dismiss, copy, or next/prev controls — so it reads as a dead-end document. The focal point is the centered title, but the eye is immediately pulled to the dense center math block and then to the bottom-right derivation; nothing indicates this belongs to a parent-facing Quran memorization app. Given the injected VIEW purpose, the focal point should be parental orchestration (child progress, next lesson, etc.), but instead the eye lands on advanced machine-learning mathematics.
strengths: The title "Polynomial Kernel" is centered, large, and immediately legible, establishing the slide topic at a glance (header bar).
The slide number "27" is clearly badged in the top-right corner, providing orientation within a deck (top-right of header bar).
The blue border cleanly contains the slide body, separating the document from the dark outer frame (main slide body).
Color-coding vector components a in red and b in blue helps distinguish the two operands across the formulas (top-left math block).

defects.description: slide body — whole region — white slide background inside a dark application frame — a surface step must get lighter as layers stack, but a white document inside dark chrome is an inversion that breaks dark-mode physics — re-theme the slide surface to match the app dark mode or declare an explicit light reader mode.

header bar — title — "Polynomial Kernel" is sans-serif while every formula is serif LaTeX — two clashing font families on one screen make the slide read like two documents glued together — unify to one family or visually separate UI chrome from math content.

math block — subscripts and superscripts (a₁, a₂, x₁²) — render at roughly half cap height, likely below the ~11px legibility floor for non-developer users — never set critical data below ~11px; enlarge math or add a zoomable viewer.
bottom-right — "2D ⇒ 6D" — smallest text on screen, set in red — reads as fine print rather than the slide's takeaway — size as a caption or promote to a hero stat.

top-right — "Remember:" callout — vertical padding inside the gray box is tighter than the surrounding math blocks — inconsistent inner padding across sibling content blocks — equalize callout padding with math block margins.

bottom row — feature-mapping objects — the row vector, matrix, and column vector each start at a different x position — a ragged left edge across one mathematical line looks like sloppy typesetting — align all three objects to a common left edge.

bottom region — full width — the derivation, the "Where:" definition, and the tall column vector are compressed into one horizontal strip; the vector nearly touches the blue border — the region is overstuffed for the pane width — split into two lines or widen the slide body.

bottom-right — "2D ⇒ 6D" — this is the conceptual punchline of the slide, yet it is tiny red corner text, visually subordinate to the derivation that supports it — promote the takeaway so it wins the eye.
top-right — "Remember:" callout — the boxed gray callout competes with the title for attention despite being secondary context — de-emphasize or relocate below the main derivation.

whole slide — content region — reads like a LaTeX worksheet pasted into an app frame; margins are uneven and the blue border feels like a page border rather than app chrome — re-compose as a proper app panel with consistent padding and a content-safe zone.
header bar — slide number "27" — the yellow badge sits flush against the top-right edge — at narrower widths it would collide with the frame edge — add right padding inside the badge container.
bottom-right — last row of the column vector — the digit "1" sits extremely close to the blue border — risks clipping at lower resolutions or narrower viewports — add right padding inside the border.

whole slide — math vs UI text — LaTeX serif math and sans-serif UI labels use different color palettes, borders, and alignment rules — two design systems merged on one screen — enforce one component language or isolate math in a dedicated viewer.
callout boxes — only one boxed callout exists ("Remember:"); no callout pattern repeats anywhere else — define a callout component or remove the box.
whole slide — interactive chrome — zero buttons, links, or navigation are visible; the screen is a static dead-end document — add back/next or dismiss controls so the user can leave the slide.

top-right — slide-number badge — looks like a static page indicator, not a clickable control, and carries no affordance to jump to slide 27 — either make it navigable or style it as purely informational.

top-right — slide-number badge — the yellow circle with "27" is the only glyph on screen and carries no icon meaning; it is isolated from any icon system — fine as a page indicator but inconsistent with an absent icon language.

math formulas — whole block — dense multi-line equations at small size; subscripts and matrix entries appear below ~11px — dense math at this scale fails legibility for non-developer users — scale up math or provide zoom.
red text "2D ⇒ 6D" — red on near-white at small size may fall below contrast requirements, and color alone carries the takeaway meaning — add a non-color cue such as bold weight or a background pill.

whole slide — content — an SVM kernel lecture slide inside an app for parents memorizing the Quran — advanced machine-learning math is the wrong register and subject matter for this audience — replace with role-appropriate content or move to a dedicated education section.
top-right callout — "Remember:" — italic instructor chatter rather than product voice; tone mismatch with a parent-facing app — align copy tone or remove.

top_3: [o|critical|high] whole slide — content — SVM math is the wrong register and subject matter for a parent-facing Quran app (§4 (o)).
[a|major|high] slide body — whole region — a white slide inside a dark frame inverts dark-mode surface elevation (§4 (a)).
[f|major|high] bottom-right — "2D ⇒ 6D" — the slide's conceptual punchline is rendered as sub-caption fine print (§4 (f)).
structural_proposal:
1. Move the SVM slide content out of the parent shell into a dedicated "Learn" or "Reference" tab; a parent dashboard should show child progress, not kernel derivations. [source: whole slide body → destination: new education tab]
2. Replace the raw LaTeX frame with a single card containing a plain-language one-line summary plus a tappable "Show math" disclosure. [source: whole slide → destination: card in the education tab]
3. Add standard reader chrome around the content: back/next controls, slide counter, and a close/dismiss action so the frame is not a dead end. [source: no interactive chrome → destination: header bar and footer of the slide viewer]
uncertainties: The injected app context (Quran memorization for parents) conflicts with the captured content (SVM lecture slide); I cannot tell whether this is a capture mismatch or an intentional education section within the app.
Navigation controls may exist off-canvas; I judged only what is visible inside the slide frame.
Exact pixel sizes for math subscripts/superscripts are estimated from the raster, not measured from CSS.
The white slide background may be an intentional "light reader mode," but nothing on screen signals that mode switch.
vocabulary_proposals: light-slide-in-dark-shell: a light-themed document surface inside a dark application frame breaks dark-mode elevation — check surface brightness against enclosing chrome, not just internal contrast.

dead-end-content-frame: a full-screen content region with no visible navigation, dismiss, or next/prev controls leaves the user with no exit path — enumerate interactive chrome before calling a screen read-only.
punchline-as-fine-print: a slide's key takeaway rendered at sub-caption size in a corner inverts information hierarchy — compare conclusion weight against supporting derivation weight.
math-font-in-ui-shell: raw LaTeX/serif math dropped into a sans UI frame creates two competing design systems — enforce one component language or isolate math in a dedicated viewer.
